subject.title: MEDIA: directive with absolute local paths outside default media roots silently fails (Telegram)

question: Should #100292 be scoped to diagnostics for dropped Telegram `MEDIA:` paths while #47002 owns configurable root expansion, or should #100292 define the root policy itself?
rationale: The current code enforces a security boundary, while accepting more host-local paths would create a public file-read/upload contract and possibly a new config surface.

options.title: Diagnostics here, roots in #47002
options.body: Keep this issue focused on warn-level per-drop reasons and optional sanitized user notices, and let #47002 or the accepted shared filesystem-roots design own root expansion.

options.title: Define root policy here
options.body: Use this issue as the canonical product/security decision for a supported media-root configuration contract.

options.title: Close as documented behavior
options.body: Declare managed roots plus the existing file-read policy and CLI workaround sufficient, and decline additional diagnostics or root expansion here.

recommendation.title: Diagnostics here, roots in #47002
recommendation.body: Keep this issue focused on warn-level per-drop reasons and optional sanitized user notices, and let #47002 or the accepted shared filesystem-roots design own root expansion.
